statusText: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES (orange). NQ is quoted at 28,871.25, down 1.76%, after printing a fourth consecutive lower low at 28,816.25 and then retracing 55 points off it. That is the first retracement of the session to hold any distance from the extreme. Two of the counterweights that degraded an hour ago have partly recovered: WTI has eased to 102.60 from a 103.81 session high, and the 10-year is not extending, quoted near 4.975% with Treasury futures marginally bid. ES is the dissenting signal, still only 3.75 points above its own session low. Tail eases one point to 25 and remains on the block boundary.
recommendation: Tail at 25 sits at the lower edge of the elevated band, exactly on the block threshold, so the mapped state remains BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The danger window runs from the current hour to 16:00 UTC, covering the remaining European session, the 13:30 UTC cash open and the first two cash hours. Conditional Tail peaks at 28 in the first full cash hour and stays six points below the strong-block threshold throughout. From 16:00 UTC the conditional path returns to the watch band and reaches the EA_ON mapping across the thin Asian hours. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: NQ prints a fourth lower low at 28,816.25 then retraces 55 points off it while WTI eases from its 103.81 high; Tail steps down to 25 and holds on the block boundary
body:
The structure that carried the prior assessment into the block band has extended once more and then, for the first time this session, met a retracement that held. NQ is quoted at 28,871.25, down 515.75 points or 1.76% against a 29,387.00 reference, as of 06:15 EDT. The session low has extended again, from 28,833.50 to 28,816.25, which is a fourth consecutive lower low. But the contract is now trading about 55 points above that low, roughly 19% of a 28,816.25 to 29,111.00 range, where an hour ago it sat eight points off the extreme at 3% of the range. Repeated extension after failed retracements is what the Tail score measures, and one retracement that holds is the first evidence against that path.

Two of the three counterweights that had degraded have partly recovered. WTI is 102.60, up 2.55%, having come off a 103.81 session high, where an hour ago it was extending to that high at up 3.36%. Brent is 107.75, up 3.00%, and also off its 108.64 high. The 10-year is quoted near 4.975% and is not extending, with Treasury futures marginally bid across the curve. The DAX has recovered to 25,439.62, down 0.50%, a full 100 points above its 25,339.10 session low. The VIX at 18.02 has made only a marginal new high at 18.17 against 18.00 an hour ago, which is deceleration rather than expansion.

ES is the dissenting signal and the reason Tail eases by one point rather than out of the band. At 7,597.50, down 0.81%, it is still only 3.75 points above its 7,593.75 session low, so the S&P contract has not participated in the Nasdaq contract's retracement. The Dow-to-Nasdaq spread remains wide, with Dow futures down 0.18% against NQ down 1.76%, which continues to describe a concentrated sector de-rating rather than index-wide liquidation.

The two drivers are unchanged and both remain unresolved. On the technology side, Anthropic's chief executive called for AI companies to slow the pace at which they advance model capabilities, and the chief executives of OpenAI and xAI said they agreed; premarket quotes cited this morning put Nvidia below -2% and Intel, AMD and Marvell each near -5% to -6%, while the Asian session saw the Kospi down 2.8%, SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics each below -3.5% and SoftBank down 13%. On the energy side, Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, carrying 4 to 5 million barrels a day, remains shut after drone strikes on 10-11 September, with the Strait of Hormuz closed since March. That combination is a stagflationary input into a week in which the Fed decides on Wednesday with roughly an 86-89% probability of a hike priced as of this assessment.

Event importance and a hawkish policy backdrop are scored into Stress at 78 and into Confidence rather than into Tail, because no post-event price path has been observed. The 13:30 UTC cash open remains the session's main checkpoint. A fifth lower low beneath 28,816.25 with shallow bounces would restore the one-way reading; a reclaim of 29,000 is the nearest conditional invalidation of the current structure.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published hours were available. Tail rose steadily through Sunday's European and US hours from 12 at 10:00 UTC to 17 by 15:00 UTC, eased to 16 at the 16:00 UTC handover, then stepped through 17, 18, 18 and 19 into the Globex reopen, crossing into the watch band at 21 and peaking at 22 in the reopen hour. Across the overnight session it was unusually stable, printing 20 in six of the following eight hours with 19 at 02:00 and 06:00 UTC, before the European open lifted it to 21 at 07:00 UTC, 23 at 08:00 UTC and 26 at 09:00 UTC, the first hour in the block band. The mapped state was EA_ON and green for the first eleven hours, WATCH and yellow for most of the overnight session with two single-hour reversions to green, and BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES with orange for the most recent hour. Dominant mode read normal through the Sunday hours, event/whipsaw for the reopen hour, mixed from 23:00 UTC onward and trend-down for the most recent hour. Confidence fell from 86 to 71 around the 16:00 UTC handover, then rebuilt steadily to 88 as live overnight price-path evidence accumulated.
outlookSummary: The danger window still begins at the current hour and runs to 16:00 UTC, covering the remaining European session, the 13:30 UTC cash open and the first two cash hours, but the projected peak is one point lower than in the prior assessment because a retracement that held has now been observed. The forecast holds at 25 on the block boundary through the European afternoon and the premarket build, steps to 27 for the opening-auction hour and peaks at 28 in the first full cash hour, the narrow single-hour top of the series and six points below the strong-block threshold. That shape reflects a concentrated AI and semiconductor de-rating against a stagflationary energy backdrop rather than index-wide liquidation. From 16:00 UTC the conditional path returns to the watch band at 24 and decays through 23 and 22 into the 20:00 UTC cash close, with a single tick back to 23 for the power hour. It falls to 20 across the CME maintenance break on a mechanical basis, holds at 21 through the Globex reopen, lifts to 22 for the Tokyo and Seoul opens where second-day AI sector reaction risk sits, then eases to the EA_ON mapping at 19 through the thinnest Asian hours. It rebuilds to 20, 21 and 22 as Europe reopens on day one of the two-day policy meeting. A fifth lower low beneath 28,816.25 with shallow pullbacks is the conditional amplifier; a reclaim of 29,000 is the nearest conditional invalidation.
